text:
maria: escalation from acme-prod — customer ran a terraform state rollback yesterday which reverted a k8s secret. Their app now gets 401 invalid_api_key when calling our hosted API. They say it worked before the rollback. Paste from their curl repro:

maria: ```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hi"}'
*   Trying 1.2.3.4...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX
> Content-Type: application/json
> 
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< 
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"The API key provided is invalid or has been revoked."}
```

maria: customer also shared these repro steps:
- rollback terraform state to 2026-02-19 commit (they say this restored secrets.tf state)
- `terraform apply` which rewrote k8s secret via helm provider
- no pods were restarted manually afterwards

ryan: first checks — ask customer for the key id (the 6-char prefix) and whether the key is hosted vs dedicated/private. If the key was rotated in the dashboard but the old value was restored into k8s, the dashboard would show the new key active and the deployed secret would be stale. Also confirm the header they're sending (Authorization vs x-api-key).

maria: customer says prefix is `sk_live_ab12cd` and it's definitely a hosted key (not a dedicated key). They pasted the helm values snippet: ```yaml
secrets:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: "sk_live_ab12cd..."
```

kevin: potential causes:
- terraform rollback restored an earlier secret value (old key) which has since been rotated or revoked
- helm/helmfile applied the value but the deployment didn't pick it up (k8s secret update doesn't always trigger a pod restart depending on how it's mounted)
- value got truncated/base64 mismatch during the pipeline (e.g., missing padding/newline)
- key scope mismatch (embeddings-only key used against generation endpoint -> 401)

maria: asked customer to run these checks and share results:
1) In dashboard: open API keys -> search for prefix `sk_live_ab12cd` -> note created_at, status, scopes
2) In cluster: `kubectl -n prod get secret redwood-key -o yaml` and confirm data.REDWOOD_API_KEY (base64) matches expected base64 of the key string
3) Quick curl from a devbox with the exact header to rule out pod network/proxy issues

ops-bot: ticket #CS-78901 created for ACME escalation :ticket: (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-78901)

jira-bot: CC'd eng-infra and eng-runtime per escalation policy

maria: customer ran the kubectl check and showed the secret base64 decodes to the older key `sk_live_z9y8xw...` (not the `ab12cd` one). They confirm the dashboard now only shows a single active key `sk_live_ab12cd` and that key was created 3 days after the terraform commit they rolled back to. So the cluster has the older key but the dashboard has the newer one.

ryan: that explains it — the cluster is pointing at a revoked/old key. Proposed remediation steps to customer (non-destructive):
- create a new API key in dashboard (or re-enable the `ab12cd` key if that fits policy)
- update k8s secret via kubectl with the exact raw value, ensuring proper base64 encoding: ```bash
kubectl -n prod create secret generic redwood-api --from-literal=REDWOOD_API_KEY='sk_live_...new...' -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/my-app
```
- verify with `curl` from a pod or their devbox: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...new..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models`

kevin: also ask them to check key scopes — if the key is restricted to embeddings only it will still 401 on generation endpoints. If they're using our SDK, remind them to clear any local env var caches and restart processes.

maria: customer applied the new key via kubectl and did `kubectl rollout restart`. They re-ran the curl and now get 200 and models list back. They confirmed app traffic is healthy again.

ryan: follow-ups for internal notes:
- add a KB entry for terraform/helm rollback cases where secret/state drift can restore revoked keys
- add an optional safety check in dashboard that warns when a key with same id is rotated within last 7 days and a cluster-applied secret matches an old value (low pri but useful)

maria: closing loop with customer, recommending rotating keys after infra rollbacks and implementing a CI step to verify secret value after deploy. Marking ticket resolved and leaving CS-78901 for postmortem/KB work. :white_check_mark:
